title: Write jmap-chat-did-guide.md
description:
Write the companion implementer guide for the DID draft. Holds all opinionated, computational, and operational content that the draft (8sgn.2) deliberately leaves to deployments. Blocked-on 8sgn.2 — do not start until the draft is committed.

## Deliverable

`jmap-chat-did-guide.md` at the top level of the repo. Non-normative companion guide, same shape as `jmap-chat-federation-guide.md` and `jmap-chat-filenode-guide.md`.

## Required structural elements

- Standard "A note on RFC 2119 keywords" wrapper at the top (per the convention established in commit 21a4bb6)
- Cross-reference table at the bottom
- Each topic section follows the established 5-subsection shape: what spec leaves open + what to decide + considerations + common patterns + recommended starting point

## Proposed sections

1. **Federation auth mechanism — concrete realization**
   - RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures: required and recommended components
   - Clock skew tolerance: starting point 300 seconds (Agora §3.5.3 reference)
   - Nonce cache TTL: starting point 600 seconds
   - Replay window and rejection codes
   - Key selection from DID document authentication relationship
   - Cross-reference: Agora protocol spec §3.5.3

2. **DID resolution and caching strategy**
   - did:web: HTTPS GET, honor cache headers, deployment floor/ceiling (5 min / 24 h starting points)
   - did:key: no caching, deterministic local derivation
   - did:plc: PLC directory resolution, log-head tracking, refresh on log advancement
   - Hard refresh on signature-verification failure (normative in the draft; expanded here)
   - Persistent resolution failure: reject auth, do not silently downgrade

3. **DID document conventions for interop**
   - Agora's two-role split (`authentication` Ed25519 + `keyAgreement` X25519) as a recommended deployment convention
   - Multi-device handling: multiple verificationMethod entries, `#device-{fingerprint}` suffix pattern
   - Why this is in the guide and not the draft

4. **Provisioning workflows**
   - `did:web` with enterprise IdP (Agora's sidecar pattern as a worked example)
   - `did:key` self-provisioning
   - `did:plc` via PLC directory and AT Protocol tooling
   - Cross-reference: Agora universal-idp-did-spec

5. **Recovery mechanisms**
   - Brief survey: recovery key, social recovery (SSS), encrypted backup (Argon2id)
   - All three are Agora's design; cite Agora §2.4 as the reference deployment
   - JMAP Chat DID itself takes no position; deployments choose

6. **Mention textual form rendering**
   - Client UX patterns for `@{did:method:value}` mentions
   - Truncation of long DIDs in UI
   - Resolution-to-display-name caching

7. **Cross-method consistency**
   - A user with multiple DIDs (e.g., did:web institutional + did:key personal): how to link them
   - When ChatContact.id and ChatContact.did refer to the same principal via different methods

8. **Security and privacy considerations expansion**
   - did:web key rotation operational practice
   - did:plc operation log monitoring
   - did:key non-rotatability and key-loss implications
   - DNS / TLS dependency for did:web in adversarial environments

## Cross-file consistency checks before close

- AGENTS.md cross-file consistency table extended to include DID-guide topics
- jmap-chat-implementer-guide.md cross-reference table extended to point at jmap-chat-did-guide.md
- README.md updated to list jmap-chat-did-guide.md in the Implementer Guides table and Repository Layout (consistent with the corpus state after 4nek)

## Acceptance criteria

- File exists at the top level of the repo
- RFC 2119 wrapper present at top
- All sections in the established 5-subsection shape
- No content duplicated from the draft (8sgn.2); cross-referenced instead
- Cross-reference table at the bottom links to draft, core implementer guide, federation guide, and Agora informative references
- AGENTS.md and implementer-guide cross-ref tables extended
- README.md updated to include the new guide
close_reason: jmap-chat-did-guide.md written. 1056 lines, 8 sections following the established 5-subsection pattern (what spec leaves open / what you must decide / considerations / common patterns / recommended starting point): federation auth concrete realization (RFC 9421 components and replay parameters), DID resolution caching strategy (per-method defaults), DID document conventions for interop (auth + keyAgreement role split, multi-device fingerprint pattern), provisioning workflows (individual/self-hosted/enterprise/AT-Protocol archetypes), recovery mechanisms (recovery key / social recovery / encrypted backup), mention textual form rendering (display-name resolution UX), cross-method consistency (per-DID ChatContacts with client-side linking), security and privacy expansion (TLS pinning, PLC operator trust, rotation cadence, audit logging, hardware key storage). RFC 2119 wrapper at top. Cross-references table at bottom links to draft anchors (capability, methods, contact-extensions, federation-auth, resolution, mentions, security), other JMAP Chat documents, informative external refs (W3C DID Core, did:web/did:key/did:plc method specs, RFC 9421), and Agora as a reference deployment (8 cross-references). Per user direction the guide treats Agora as one example among possibilities, not as canonical — operational patterns are framed as JMAP Chat DID's own guidance with Agora cited where applicable. jmap-chat-implementer-guide.md cross-ref table extended with DID-guide row. README.md updated: Implementer Guides table and Repository Layout block both include the new guide. AGENTS.md cross-file consistency table was already updated in 8sgn.2.
